name: Beard balm

lead: Beard balm is a thicker mixture of butters and beeswax, often with oils, that conditions the beard and holds its shape. It is used after washing to control flyaways and shape the outline.
It is a styling and conditioning aid and is not reported to affect growth. No clinical research on beard balms was found.

paras: Waxes form a light film that holds hairs in place while butters and oils soften and add moisture. Warmth from the hands makes the product spread through the beard.

Heavy use can leave residue, weigh the beard down and clog skin if not washed out. Fragrance and nut-based ingredients can irritate or trigger allergies. Effects last until washing, and the claims are limited to appearance and feel.

lead: Beard balm is a thick grooming product made from butters and beeswax, often with oils, applied to a clean beard to condition it and hold its shape.[1] Users apply it to tame flyaways and define the outline. It does not alter growth.

No clinical research on beard balms was found. The beard itself is a secondary sexual characteristic studied by evolutionary and dermatology researchers, but that literature concerns facial hair, not the product.[2]

paras: Balms are firmer than beard oils. The wax component is described as forming a light film that holds hairs in place, while butters and oils soften and add moisture; warmth from the hands spreads the product.

Wikipedia describes the beard as androgen-dependent facial hair whose social meaning has varied across cultures and eras, and notes research on how beards affect perceived age, dominance and attractiveness.[1] Those studies do not test grooming products.
Heavy use can leave residue, weigh down the beard and clog skin if not washed out. Fragrance and nut-based ingredients can irritate or trigger allergy in some people. Effects last until washing.
